title: Exact run from a bounded execution
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $w,e$ be finite binary lists, let $\rho:\{0,\ldots,10\}\to\mathbb{N}$ be register values, and let $p,B,C\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every output list $o$ there is a time $t\le B$ at which the 11-register program associated with $M$, started at its initial label with all registers and the input position zero and output $o$, is halted with register values $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ followed by $e$. If $B\le C$, then after exactly $C$ steps, starting from that initial configuration with empty output, the program is halted with register values $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $e$.

$\rho$ assigns a natural number to each of the 11 registers
